reason: I'll start with the artery: the picture shows the lining fitting inside its strong elastic wall.
expectation: I expect a lined artery whose wall can stretch and spring back with the pulse.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and cells also clearly belong together for exchange, but I want to build the outward route first.

effect: The artery is lined and carries blood away from the heart, completing the first goal.
reaction: The result matched the picture I expected.
reason: I'll build the exchange route next: the thin capillaries are shown close to body cells.
expectation: I expect capillaries positioned near cells so materials can pass between blood and the cells.

alternatives.reason: The vein also needs a lining, but I want to follow the route outward toward the cells first.

effect: The capillary bed shows oxygen and nutrients moving toward cells and carbon dioxide moving toward blood, while blood cells stay inside.
reaction: The different directions of exchange made the capillaries' job clearer.
reason: I'll line the venous wall to start the remaining return-route goal; its picture shows an unlined interior.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, though it may still need the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the artery to the capillaries also follows the blood's route, but I want to prepare the return route first.

effect: The lined veins point toward the heart; they still need valves for the return-route goal.
reason: I'll add the valve flaps to complete the return route; their picture shows them stopping backward flow.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the arteries and capillaries also makes sense, but I want to finish preparing the veins first.

effect: The veins now have valves, and the picture shows muscle squeezing helping move blood forward. The remaining goal is to join the routes.
reaction: The muscle's role was a useful surprise.
reason: I'll connect the arteries to the capillary bed as the only offered combination toward joining the routes.
expectation: I expect a route from the arteries into the capillaries; it may still need to connect to the veins.

effect: The artery now branches into capillaries, with open ends ready for the return route.
reason: I'll connect the venous return to complete the route; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the capillaries to connect to veins carrying blood back toward the heart.

effect: The completed network connects arteries, capillaries and veins into a route away from and back toward the heart.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate routes joined.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile because it showed which materials move between blood and body cells, and that blood cells stay inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the vein was the least interesting part: it was predictable after lining the artery, though it helped prepare the return route.

surprise.text: I was surprised that a contracting muscle can squeeze a vein while its valves help blood move forward.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures made the fittings clear. The final connections were the only offered combinations, though, rather than discoveries of compatibility.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the separate vessel jobs come together was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the next body system connects.
